About the RoleWe are looking for a high-energy Enrichment Teacher who can command a room and keep it buzzing. This is a generalist role. Across a single day you might lead a gym class, run a music and art circle, coach a toddler through a first tumble, and keep our Afternoon Club moving until pickup. We're looking for a big presence, a strong voice, and the stamina to bring energy and structure to every class, every hour. What You’ll DoLead the room. Take charge of gym, movement, music, art, STEM, and sports classes for children ages 2 to 6, keeping every class active, structured, and fun from the first minute to the last.Bring the energy. Set the tone with a strong voice and a big presence. You keep children engaged, moving, and excited, and you hold that energy across a full afternoon.Stay two steps ahead. Notice behavior early and redirect it before it escalates, hold clear and consistent expectations, and keep transitions quick so no minute is wasted.Run Afternoon Club. At several locations you will lead our after-school program through 6:00 pm: a fast-paced mix of gym, dance, sports, art, and more, where children move from activity to activity and families pick up throughout the afternoon.Partner with families. Give parents clear daily updates on their child’s wins and challenges, building a bridge between school and home.What Success Looks LikeA safe, joyful, high-energy classroom where every child is engaged and thriving.Behavior noticed and redirected early, with calm and consistent expectations.Smooth, quick transitions that keep every minute of class productive.Trust-based relationships with students, families, and your team.100% compliance with all Department of Health requirements. What We’re Looking ForPresence and energy. You are comfortable being the most animated person in the room. You engage a group of young children quickly and keep your energy high across a full day or a long afternoon.Classroom leadership. You notice and redirect behavior calmly and early, and you hold structure without losing the fun.Experience. 1 to 2+ years teaching children ages 2 to 6 (camp, pre-k, after-school, daycare, or enrichment). Comfort leading gym and movement classes matters most; experience in music, dance, gymnastics, sports, or yoga is a plus.Education. A High School Diploma or equivalent is required. An Associate’s or Bachelor’s in Early Childhood, or study in progress, is preferred.Stamina. This is an active, on-your-feet role. You will be moving, spotting, and performing for most of your shift.Physical exam and background checks are required for this position. What to Expect in the ProcessEvery candidate leads a short read-aloud as part of the interview. Come ready to run a few minutes of a class as if we are your students. We want to see your energy, your presence, and how you hold and lead a group. Why You’ll Love Working HereCareer Investment: Tuition Reimbursement Program for full-time team members.Comprehensive Care: Dental, and Vision coverage, plus a 401(k) Plan with Company Contribution.The Extras: Commuter programs, discounted fitness memberships, and more.Physical DemandsThe role involves standing, walking, sitting, constant movement, and occasional climbing. If you need accommodation in completing the application, please contact interview@nykidsclub.com.The pay rate for this role is $20.00/hour.

jobs.description: Employer: ETC Phoenix School Expires: 10/13/2026 Date posted: September 27, 2026Pay: $3,500.00 - $4,500.00 per monthJob description:OverviewWe are seeking a passionate and dedicated Special Education Teacher to serve students in kindergarten through first grade, fostering an inclusive and supportive learning environment. This role offers an exciting opportunity to make a meaningful impact on young learners with diverse needs, including those with autism spectrum disorders, developmental disabilities, and other neurodevelopmental conditions. The ideal candidate will bring energy, creativity, and a strong commitment to advancing early childhood education and special education practices. You will collaborate closely with families, therapists, and other educators to develop individualized learning plans that promote growth, independence, and confidence in every student. This paid position is designed to inspire both students and colleagues alike, ensuring a vibrant classroom experience that champions every child's potential.About our SchoolWe are a small inclusive Christian school. As a young school, we are looking for people that can grow with us. We started in January 2025 with 8 students and have developed a unique program that is centered around individualization, social and life skills, and developing the child as a whole. We currently have about 20 students and continue to grow!About the PositionK-1 inclusive classroom3-6 students (depending on the day- some students are parttime)School hours are 9-3pm, contract hours 8:45-3:15Occasional afterschool activities (talent show, open houses, etc.)ResponsibilitiesDesign and implement engaging lesson plans tailored to the unique needs of K-1 students with disabilities.Develop and monitor individual academic and social goals. While we don't have IEPs, we still track progress.Utilize evidence-based behavioral therapy techniques and behavior management strategies to support positive behavior and social-emotional development.Collaborate effectively with speech therapists, occupational therapists, behavior specialists, parents, and other professionals to provide comprehensive support for each student’s development.Maintain professional parent communication.SkillsProven experience working with children in early childhood education settings, particularly within special education or preschool environments.Strong knowledge of childhood development principles, early intervention strategies, and classroom management techniques for students with disabilities.Expertise in teaching students with developmental disabilities, autism spectrum disorders support, and neurodevelopmental disorder accommodations.Excellent communication skills for effective parent-teacher collaboration and team coordination; ability to convey complex information clearly and compassionately.Familiarity with special education law (IDEA), IEP processes, instructional modifications, and behavior management plans tailored for diverse learners.Preferred ExperienceLicensed teacher certificationExperience in early childhood education (preschool, kindergarten, elementary)Experience with special educationJoin us in creating a dynamic classroom environment where every child’s potential is unlocked through innovative teaching methods and heartfelt dedication! This role offers the rewarding chance to shape young minds while working alongside a collaborative team committed to excellence in special education.Benefits:Health insurance Experience:Teaching: 1 year (Preferred) License/Certification:Teaching License (Preferred) Work Location: In person

jobs.description: Employer: Mindful Body Therapy and Wellness Expires: 10/13/2026 Mindful Body Therapy & Wellness focuses on creating a safe and understanding environment for individuals seeking mental health support. Our clinicians tailor treatments to individual strengths using a variety of therapeutic approaches such as cognitive behavioral therapy, narrative therapy, and mindfulness. We address diverse mental health concerns such as eating disorders, anxiety, depression, trauma, and life transitions to help individuals achieve their recovery goals. This is a full-time role primarily based in Andover, MA, with the flexibility for some remote work. ResponsibilitiesThe primary goal of a clinician is to provide therapy to clients while operating in a team environment. Therefore, a Clinician is responsible for:Conducting a minimum of 25 therapy sessions per weekCompleting thorough assessments of clients' mental health needs and develop personalized treatment plansCollaborating with clients to establish goals and monitor progress throughout therapyEmploying evidence-based therapeutic techniques to address a range of mental health concernsMaintaining accurate and up-to-date client records in compliance with ethical and legal standardsCollaborating with other healthcare professionals, such as psychiatrists, social workers, and case managers, to ensure comprehensive care for clientsOffering crisis intervention and support to clients in urgent situationsParticipating in regular supervision, training, and professional development activities to enhance clinical skillsUpholding ethical standards and confidentiality in all aspects of therapy practiceAttending and engaging in staff meetings, collaboration meetings, and group supervision Additional related tasks may be added to this description based on the needs of the practice. Required Skills and QualificationsA Clinician must be working toward or hold licensure in a Social Work, Counseling, or a related field in addition to:Strong knowledge of therapeutic modalities and interventionsAbility to work effectively with individuals of all agesSkills in conducting assessments and developing treatment plansProficiency in crisis intervention and trauma-informed careExcellent interpersonal and communication skillsAbility to work independently and as part of a collaborative teamA welcoming personalityEmpathetic, non-judgmental, and culturally sensitive approach to therapyCommitment to continuous learningExperience working with eating disorders, preferred Clinician BenefitsHealth and Dental insurancePaid time offPaid sick timeCovered cost of a Psychology Today accountContinuing Education Unit reimbursementInvestment matching Flexible work arrangements including remote work and flexible schedulingProfessional development opportunities such as group collaboration, outside provider presentations, conferencesAdministrative assistanceSupervision

jobs.description: Employer: University of San Francisco Expires: 10/13/2026 Associate Vice Provost for Student Financial Services University of San Francisco R0011770 USF Hilltop Campus Job Title:Associate Vice Provost for Student Financial Services Job Summary:The associate vice provost will be responsible for assuring compliance with all applicable federal and state regulations and all effective and responsible business practices; provide information and support on federal and state issues to the Office of the President, the general counsel, the Vice President for SEM and will represent the University on the state and federal level when called upon; lead proactively, employing leveraging and accessing financial aid models to shape an increasingly competitive undergraduate applicant pool and supporting enrollment and retention of undergraduate and graduate students with an exemplary student service model; create and support financial literacy initiatives to educate the financial services team, students, families and other important constituents within the campus community; and supervise a staff of approximately 21 full-time positions, including professional and support staff. This leader will have not only a curiosity that inspires innovation but also the analytical and intellectual abilities to evaluate the effectiveness of financial aid and student accounts policies and procedures created to support student enrollment and success. The associate vice provost will have superior communication skills, including strong listening skills and the ability to make connections across the University in order to promote open dialogue and the sharing of information to promote common goals. The associate vice provost will lead a campus team that is collaborative, committed and supportive, operating with a strong sense of mission, community and purpose. USF needs a compelling advocate for liberal arts and sciences and professional studies who is able to appreciate its identity as a leading Jesuit Catholic urban university and communicate the University's fundamental values, including a focus on student success, diversity and civic and community engagement. USF needs a leader in student financial services who is experienced in leading conversations with students and families who are increasingly assessing the cost and affordability of private higher education. Full Job Description: Job Description Responsibilities include but are not limited to the following: • Leading USF in the development of a creative 21st century financial aid program to enhance communication around financial aid, verification, scholarship and loan procedures;• Supporting the acquisition and implementation of new systems, tools and technology to empower financial aid and student accounts in optimizing operations that include responsiveness to meet both the financial aid and literacy needs of current and new students;• Analyze quantitative data with an experienced eye to shape strategic directions with integrity;• Communicate effectively and build multifaceted educational forums on campus and in the community to translate language of financial aid policies, procedures and knowledge to students and families;• Assess and reassess regularly the effectiveness of USF policies around financial aid programs and make appropriate adjustments to lead an effort that is proactive and responsive to market forces and University needs;• Assure compliance with all applicable federal and state regulations and effective and efficient management of all University, state and federal student aid programs;• Serve as a public face of and a key spokesperson for the University and maintain excellent relationships in state and national conversations on student financial aid needs and the changing post-secondary education environment at professional meetings and consortia. Professional Qualifications and Personal Qualities • Proven effectiveness and expertise in financial aid: Expertise in creating systems to enhance student service in student financial services; Significant experience participating in leadership and management within student financial services; the University seeks a leader who shows genuine enjoyment in leading the student financial services function which supports the institutional goals and objectives; and an understanding of best practices nationally in the dynamic and changing landscape that directs state and federal funding.• Analytical strength: Experience in developing financial aid models in support of strategic enrollment management; the capacity for analytical thinking and ability to consider broadly the impact of admissions and financial aid outcomes on the University as a whole; proven experience in managing complex budgets; and experience in assessment of effectiveness of financial aid funding models.• Willingness to embrace the University's mission and values: A strong grasp and support for the central ethos of Jesuit Catholic education, mission and character; and the ability to advocate effectively for it; and the personal and intellectual qualities expected of members of the University community.• Vision, leadership, and communication skills: Vision for the future of student financial services at USF; highly attuned understanding of motivation; and the capacity to work effectively with those who have an interest in the process of attracting, shaping and retaining USF student body.• Inclusive leadership style: Empower seasoned and new staff to execute decisions with good judgment and responsiveness; support the already excellent synergy and cohesive working relationship that exists between student accounts and financial aid; readiness to be part of the Strategic Enrollment Management's senior team; and ability to act as an expert in student financial services, leading community-wide conversations and working in unison to execute the vision of University leadership.• Technological sophistication: The ability to understand the potential value of technological innovations and to lead the process of harnessing emerging technologies for best use within all student financial service and strategic enrollment management functions.• Exceptional personal qualities: Superb interpersonal and communication skills; an ability to join in partnership with colleagues, faculty, students, parents, alumni and trustees to advance the enrollment effort; articulateness; student-centered; a sense of mission and engagement; honesty and candor; a personal presence that is warm, active and engaged; exhibits resilience and a positive attitude; and a sense of humor.• Credentials: Graduate degree is strongly preferred; the successful candidate should have a record of progressively responsible and complex student financial services related experiences and at least five years at a senior level leading this unit, preferably within an operation focused on strategic enrollment management. Full-Time/Part-Time:Full time Pay Rate:Salary Salary Range :$170,000 - 190,000 annualized; commensurate with experience To apply, visit https://apptrkr.com/6638630. The University of San Francisco is located in the heart of one of the world’s most innovative and diverse cities, and is home to a vibrant academic community of students and faculty who achieve excellence in their fields. Its diverse student body enjoys direct access to faculty, small classes and outstanding opportunities in the city itself. USF is San Francisco's first university, and its Jesuit Catholic mission helps ignite a student’s passion for social justice and a desire to “Change the World From Here.” For more information, visit http://www.usfca.edu. jobs.description: Employer: Colorado College Expires: 10/14/2026 Assistant Professor of Economics and Business To apply, please visit: https://apptrkr.com/7330126 Job Title: Assistant Professor of Economics and Business Position Status: Tenure-Track Academic Rank: Assistant Professor Department: Economics and Business Campus Location: Main Campus Job Summary The Department of Economics and Business at Colorado College invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor of Economics and Business with specialization in marketing, to begin Fall 2027. The department offers four undergraduate degrees which reflect our interdisciplinary approach to economics and business: (1) Business, Economics, and Society; (2) Economics; (3) International Political Economy; and (4) Mathematical Economics. We engage students in immersive pedagogy via field trips, community-engaged work, and intensive group projects. Responsibilities for this position entail teaching five courses annually plus advising students' senior theses, which counts as a sixth course. Faculty are also expected to maintain an active research program and engage in college service. No experience with such courses is required, only willingness to learn • An active research agenda aimed at peer-reviewed publications commensurate with selective liberal arts institutions (for reference, faculty cvs are https://www.coloradocollege.edu/academics/dept/economics/people/department-faculty.html; college requirements for tenure are found https://www.coloradocollege.edu/offices/humanresources/people-practices/handbooks/facultyhandbook.pdf on pp. 16-18; the department statement on scholarship is found https://cctigers-my.sharepoint.com/:b:/g/personal/crader_coloradocollege_edu/EemhqXVZkJ9OrEmBcQLmp0gBC04KyT7NpsaVspa7VxB0QA?e=8ScNfa.) Colorado College is a nationally recognized, residential liberal arts and sciences college enrolling approximately 2,100 students from across the US and around the world. The College, located on a 99-acre campus in Colorado Springs, is distinguished by its immersive learning and pedagogy made possible by the Block Plan, in which professors teach, and students take, one course at a time. Each block is three and a half weeks long, allowing for unique teaching and learning strategies. Professors have a six-block teaching duty in the eight-block year, where one of the six blocks may be assigned to supervising senior and independent projects where the work is spread out across the year rather than completed in a conventional block. Colorado College actively promotes a dynamic and inclusive environment in which students and employees of diverse backgrounds, cultures, and perspectives can learn and work. Read more about our the College's commitment in our https://www.coloradocollege.edu/offices/adei/ and the strategic plan "https://www.coloradocollege.edu/offices/adei/strategic-plan.html." jobs.title: Associate Vice President of Healthy Living at YMCA of the Triangle
jobs.description: Employer: YMCA of the Triangle Expires: 10/14/2026 POSITION SUMMARY: Under the supervision of the Vice President of Operations and Healthy Living and in cooperation with YMCA staff, the Associate VP of Healthy Living ensures branches deliver a safe and high-quality member experience that is designed to meet the unique member programming and health and well-being goals of participants that the Y of the Triangle serves. The candidate must be able to apply critical thinking abilities and utilize effective communication skills to develop strategic plans and effective messages to support the YMCA of the Triangle’s Healthy Living efforts. The AVP of Healthy Living will partner with Branch Membership and Healthy Living Departments across the Association to develop curriculum and deliver engaging, high quality and consistent wellness programs that increase member engagement, retention and growth of revenue. The incumbent will also focus on connecting members to small membership/wellness/fitness communities within our Y. They will be responsible for managing such functions in accordance with the stated mission and polices established by the administrative staff, governing committees and Board of Directors of the YMCA. ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS: Strategy, Programs & Growth Provides vision and leadership for the YMCA of the Triangle’s Membership Experience. Accountable for program design implementation for existing and future program models and ensuring program fidelity. Responsible for developing, leading and supporting the YMCA of the Triangle’s Membership and Wellness/Fitness Programs – focusing on group fitness, personal/small group training and member onboarding – in collaboration and partnership with Membership, Healthy Living Directors, ARC and branch leadership. Leads innovation, collaboration and program integration among Membership, Wellness, Personal Training and Group Fitness Programs. Responsible for developing, leading and supporting the YMCA of the Triangle’s Personal Training and Small Group Training Program in collaboration and partnership with Healthy Living Directors and branch leadership. Responsibility for leading efforts with Healthy Living Directors and branch leadership to grow revenue of Personal Training/Small Group programs Leads the planning, project management and execution of association-wide program launches, service enhancements, curriculum updates and strategic initiatives, ensuring projects are delivered on time, within scope and aligned with organizational goals. Serves as executive sponsor and project leader for enterprise Healthy Living and Membership initiatives, coordinating cross-functional teams, resources, timelines, communications and implementation plans across the Association. Research, report and make decisions based on analytics of the latest trends and development in the membership and fitness industry. Operations, Performance & Continuous Improvement Monitors and tracks all data related to membership and wellness programs across the association. Develops strategies to close gaps identified in relevant data related to the various program areas: Membership, Group Fitness, Personal Training/Small Group Training and Equipment. Explores ways, through data-driven decisions, to enhance and promote the quality of the association’s membership and wellness programs with a focus on membership growth and retention. Monitors and tracks all data related to group fitness, personal training and small group training across the association including branch reservations systems, participation numbers and quality/experience of class participants – to inform schedules, offerings and growth opportunities. Works in collaboration with IT to create tools in PowerBI. Develops project charters, implementation plans, success metrics and stakeholder communication strategies for major operational and strategic initiatives. Works with Branch and Association Operation teams to evaluate group wellness/fitness environments (i.e. studio lighting, sound systems, supplemental equipment, stage, flooring and color schemes) and makes recommendations to enhance the experience/program. People Leadership, Training & Team Development Supervises, coaches and leads the Healthy Living/Membership Experience team comprised of Association Director of Member Experience, Association Director of Wellness Experience and Association Equipment Coordinator. Leads the collaboration with the Association Director of Community Health and the Association Director of Membership Experience and Association Director Wellness Experience to: Support the innovation, pathway, engagement and onboarding of members to group wellness programs. Support the pathway, engagement and onboarding of members into Community health programs. Support all members in their journey to reach their health and wellness goals. Works collaboratively with the Operational Vice Presidents, ARC Department Heads, Employee Resource Groups and Branch leadership to: Provide on-going leadership and direction to membership and wellness professionals Ensure consistent on-boarding for new membership, wellness and group fitness full-time directors and staff Ensure program quality, standards and expectations in related areas that meet the needs of our existing membership in supporting their health and well-being goals Provides leadership and supports the work of the Membership (Membership Directors) and Wellness Teams (Healthy Living Directors) at branches and other cross-departmental teams related to member experience. Leads and facilitates cross-functional project teams, steering committees and workgroups, ensuring accountability, alignment and successful execution of strategic priorities. Supports recruitment and selection of wellness staff across multiple dimensions of diversity, supporting branches to acquire and develop high-quality Adult Associates, Healthy Living Directors, group fitness instructors, personal trainers and wellness coaches. Actively audits classes and programs for quality, instructor coaching opportunities and curriculum delivery - working during branch peak hours, which include mornings, evenings and weekends. Supports the Association’s Quarterly Launch for new Group Wellness/Fitness Programs. This includes branch team practices, tracking allocations and supporting all education/curriculum efforts of new program materials for the Y. Designs and leads an onboarding system for wellness, personal training and group fitness for current and new YMCA members. Provides strategic oversight and project governance for the Personal Training and Small Group Training portfolio, including planning, implementation, evaluation and continuous improvement efforts. Partnerships, Resources & Communication Leads enterprise equipment planning and capital projects, including needs assessment, budgeting, vendor coordination, implementation planning, stakeholder communication and project execution. Works collaboratively with the CFO, COO, VP of Finance, VP of Healthy Living creating the annual equipment budget. In partnership with the Association Equipment Coordinator, leads wellness floor design and fitness equipment asset management. Negotiates contracts, builds and maintains relationships with equipment vendors who supply products and services for wellness, personal training and group fitness programs. Leads the Personal Training and Small Group Training Project Team. Leads and directs the implementation and ongoing integration of fitness engagement technology platforms, including Fisikal, NetGym, Myzone and Evolt, while supporting the strategic vision and direction of the YMCA mobile app. Ensures brand compliance within Association standards through marketing and communication efforts. Works in partnership with marketing & communications department to create tailored marketing collateral for membership/group wellness/fitness/exercise for both internal and external audiences. Maintains regular, clear and concise communication within area of responsibility. jobs.title: Program Associate, AmeriCorps Workforce Development at National Council on Aging
jobs.description: Employer: National Council on Aging Expires: 10/14/2026 Join Our Mission. Shape the Future. At NCOA, we are on a mission to create the conditions for all to age well in America—today and into the future. Every day, we work to improve the lives of millions of older adults through innovative programs, trusted advocacy, and meaningful partnerships that advance health, economic security, and equity. We are seeking a dynamic and collaborative Program Associate, AmeriCorps Workforce Development to bring their expertise, passion, and commitment to help drive our mission forward. This team member will play a pivotal role in supporting the AmeriCorps Seniors Workforce Development Senior Demonstration Program by coordinating participant services, strengthening community and employer partnerships, and helping older adults build the skills and experience needed to pursue meaningful employment opportunities. The ideal candidate is an organized and relationship-focused program professional who thrives on supporting participants, building community relationships, and coordinating multiple priorities to help older adults successfully navigate training, volunteer service, and pathways to employment. They will embrace and exemplify NCOA's core values of Caring for All, Collaboration, Innovation, Integrity, and Respect, fostering a culture of excellence while helping ensure that every older adult has the opportunity to age with dignity, purpose, and security. If you are ready to make a lasting difference while leading with purpose, we invite you to join our team. POSITION SUMMARY The Program Associate, AmeriCorps Workforce Development plays a key role in supporting the planning, coordination, and implementation of workforce development initiatives within the Center for Economic Well-Being (CEW). This includes providing program, participant, and operational support for the AmeriCorps Seniors Workforce Development Senior Demonstration Program (SDP) activities in Wheeling, West Virginia. Working both independently and collaboratively, the Program Associate partners with internal staff, community organizations, employers, training providers, and volunteers to support successful program implementation and advance workforce development goals. Working closely with the AmeriCorps program team, the Program Associate supports AmeriCorps Seniors volunteers throughout the West Virginia Northern Panhandle, western Pennsylvania, and eastern Ohio by coordinating participant recruitment, volunteer service, training, mentoring, and employment readiness activities for adults age 55 and older. The Program Associate builds relationships with the local business community to expand workforce opportunities for older adults and support participants in obtaining permanent employment. This position emphasizes providing quality volunteer experiences and specialized training that prepare older adults for permanent employment. About the AmeriCorps Seniors Workforce Development Senior Demonstration Program (SDP): The AmeriCorps Seniors Workforce Development Senior Demonstration Program (SDP) is funded by AmeriCorps Seniors and supports older adults in obtaining permanent employment in skilled labor and professional careers. Grantee organizations—including NCOA—provide: Training and/or certification for employment, and support such as mentorship, coaching, transportation, and other forms of support. Mentoring and/or coaching in regular increments, including during pre- and post-employment placement. A competitive stipend to remove barriers for older adults’ service. Positions at this level typically report to an associate director or director and require experience supporting projects and managing tasks or deliverables. Incumbents are required to exercise judgement within their scope of work based on defined guidelines. Incumbents generally have one or more years of experience in their discipline and a bachelor’s degree or the equivalent, as well as substantive experience at this level. Graduate level degrees may be considered in lieu of experience. *This grant-funded position is a short-term, temporary position that is funded through June 30, 2028, and designed to be filled by a W-2 employee. KEY RESPONSIBILITIESCoordinate day-to-day implementation of the AmeriCorps Seniors Workforce Development Senior Demonstration Program (SDP) to support participant success and achievement of grant objectives.Serve as a case manager for enrolled AmeriCorps Seniors volunteers to provide a path to successful program completion. This includes:Recruiting volunteers and matching them to the appropriate volunteer station.Ensuring accurate data collection and entry into the database.Conducting weekly check-ins with AmeriCorps volunteers.Supporting volunteers who need additional digital literacy training by providing them access to standard curriculum. Enrolling volunteers in appropriate specialized training courses and coordinating any certification testing needed to support their employment objectives.Identifying job opportunities for AmeriCorps Seniors volunteers who have completed their training, curriculum, and volunteer service experience and supporting their transition to permanent employment.Maintaining contact with volunteers who have exited the program to follow up on and track their employment status and income.Support the development and implementation of participant recruitment strategies to maintain consistent enrollment levels and a pipeline of prospective volunteers.Identify appropriate volunteer training sites and maintain communication with partner organizations to support positive training and volunteer experiences for AmeriCorps Seniors volunteers. Work with volunteer station partners to identify service opportunities that meet organizational needs while supporting volunteers’ employment and training goals, including opportunities for job shadowing and skill development. Customize volunteer opportunities to meet the employment training needs of each volunteer and create an individualized training plan for each volunteer. Monitor assigned program activities, participant data, and progress toward performance measures to support quality service delivery, achievement of grant objectives, and compliance with applicable grant and program requirements.Collaborate regularly in-office with other AmeriCorps Workforce Development and Program Evaluation team members to coordinate program activities, share information, and support successful grant implementation.Maintain confidentiality and comply with all applicable AmeriCorps and NCOA program standards, procedures, and data security requirements. Serve as an ambassador for NCOA’s mission, programs, and social impact goals by building and maintaining positive relationships with employers, community organizations, public and private agencies, and other external stakeholders to promote awareness of AmeriCorps Seniors, workforce development initiatives, and older worker issues.Participate in team meetings, work planning, trainings, community events, performance monitoring, and continuous improvement activities to support program and departmental goals.Conduct site visits, attend conferences and community events, participate in partner meetings, and engage in other business travel as needed to support participant services, partner relationships, program implementation, and organizational priorities.Complete required annual National Service Criminal History Check (NSCHC) training and other trainings as required by AmeriCorps and NCOA. Perform other responsibilities as assigned. PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE/QUALIFICATIONSBachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of education and experience.1-3 years of relevant experience in program coordination, program support, or a similar role required; experience in workforce development, employment and training, human services, job readiness, or a related field preferred.Demonstrated ability to coordinate projects, manage multiple priorities, and meet deadlines while maintaining strong organizational skills and attention to detail.Strong verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills, with the ability to build effective relationships with participants, employers, community organizations, and other stakeholders.Ability to provide participant-centered case management and support, maintain ongoing participant engagement and follow-up, and respond effectively to individual participant needs.Experience supporting nonprofit or grant-funded programs, including tracking deliverables, organizing reports, monitoring activities, and assisting with day-to-day program operations, preferred.Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite and experience learning and utilizing web-based data management systems, such as Salesforce or similar platforms. Demonstrated ability to work independently while contributing effectively within a collaborative, cross-functional team environment. Experience working with older adults, diverse communities, minority populations, low-income communities, or other underserved populations strongly preferred. Familiarity with workforce development resources and employer networks in the Northern Panhandle of West Virginia, eastern Ohio, or western Pennsylvania, including experience networking with public agencies and community organizations at the local level, preferred. Ability and willingness to travel regularly throughout the service area to volunteer stations, partner sites, and community locations as needed, including occasional same-day or time-sensitive travel. PHYSICAL DEMANDS The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. Frequently required to sit or use a standing desk. Occasionally required to walk. Occasionally required to reach with hands and arms. Frequently required to talk or listen. Occasionally required to bend, lift or climb stairs.Occasionally required to lift light weights (less than 25 pounds). WORK ENVIRONMENT The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate.Primarily office-based in Wheeling, WV, with a hybrid schedule. Regular travel throughout the service area is required for partner meetings, events, and other partner engagements. Ready to Make an Impact? If you are a collaborative, mission-driven professional with a passion for creating meaningful change, we encourage you to apply. Interested candidates should submit a cover letter and resume through the application link provided. Applications submitted without a cover letter will not be considered. Please note that we are unable to accept phone calls regarding this position. NCOA is committed to providing competitive and equitable compensation. The salary range published in this job posting reflects the market range for positions based in the Wheeling, WV region. Because NCOA employs staff in multiple states, compensation may vary based on an employee's primary work location through our geographic pay structure. Geographic differentials are established using regional labor market data to ensure competitive and equitable pay across locations. Final starting salary will be determined based on the employee's work location, relevant experience, education, qualifications, and internal equity. NCOA is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer and is committed to fostering an equitable, inclusive, and respectful workplace where everyone has the opportunity to thrive.

jobs.title: Sign Language Staff Interpreter at VersAbility Resources
jobs.description: Employer: VersAbility Resources Expires: 10/14/2026 About VersAbility ResourcesVersAbility Resources is a nonprofit organization based in Hampton, Virginia, dedicated to empowering people of all abilities to thrive. For more than 70 years, we have provided innovative employment, workforce development, residential, community living, and business services that promote independence, inclusion, and opportunity.Our team is passionate about making a meaningful impact by helping individuals achieve their personal and professional goals while delivering high-quality services to our community, business partners, and government customers. At VersAbility, you'll join a mission-driven organization where your work changes lives and contributes to stronger, more inclusive communities.Role OverviewThis is more than a new position—it is an important investment in communication access and inclusion at VersAbility Resources. VersAbility Resources is excited to welcome our first Sign Language Staff Interpreter, a permanent role dedicated to strengthening communication access for our Deaf and hard-of-hearing employees across the organization.Rather than relying solely on interpreting support for individual meetings or events, this position creates consistent, ongoing access to a professional who understands our employees, our workplaces, and the environments in which our teams work. For our Deaf and hard-of-hearing employees, that means greater continuity and access during orientations, training, meetings, workplace conversations, and other important moments throughout their employment experience.The Sign Language Staff Interpreter will provide professional American Sign Language (ASL)/English interpreting services across VersAbility locations, including Government Contract sites throughout Hampton Roads, while also providing virtual support to employees at geographically dispersed locations such as San Diego and Hawaii. This individual will help facilitate accurate, effective, and culturally responsive communication while respecting each employee's autonomy, communication preferences, confidentiality, and individual needs.If you are an experienced interpreter who believes communication access is essential to an inclusive workplace and wants the opportunity to become a trusted, consistent part of an organization rather than moving from assignment to assignment, this is an opportunity to make a lasting impact.What You'll DoProvide accurate, real-time, two-way interpretation between spoken English and ASL.Interpret workplace conversations, meetings, orientations, training, administrative discussions, healthcare-related interactions, technical information, and other organizational communications.Convey the complete meaning, intent, tone, context, and emotional nuance of communication rather than relying on word-for-word interpretation.Adapt interpreting approaches based on individual communication preferences, language proficiency, cultural considerations, and assignment needs.Provide interpreting support for regularly scheduled New Employee Orientation (NEO) and other organizational meetings, training, and events.Travel to VersAbility locations and Government Contract sites throughout Hampton Roads to provide on-site interpreting support.Provide virtual interpreting services for geographically dispersed VersAbility locations, including locations such as Hawaii and San Diego.Prepare for assignments by reviewing materials and becoming familiar with relevant terminology, acronyms, technical information, and subject matter.Collaborate with Deaf interpreters and other hearing interpreters during team-interpreting assignments.Coordinate appropriately with employees, managers, Human Resources, Supported Employment staff, and other stakeholders to support successful interpreting assignments.Maintain confidentiality, impartiality, professional boundaries, and ethical standards consistent with applicable professional interpreting standards, including the RID Code of Professional Conduct.Maintain required schedules, records, certifications, credentials, security clearances, and professional qualifications.Participate in continuing education, professional development, meetings, and required training.Perform other related duties as assigned.QualificationsRequiredHigh school diploma or GED equivalent.Minimum of one (1) year of professional ASL/English interpreting experience.Virginia Quality Assurance Screening (VQAS) Level III or above.Advanced proficiency in American Sign Language and spoken English.Strong understanding of Deaf culture, hearing culture, cultural norms, communication preferences, and culturally responsive interpreting practices.Knowledge of professional interpreting ethics, confidentiality, impartiality, professional boundaries, and the RID Code of Professional Conduct.Valid state-issued driver's license with an acceptable driving record.Ability and willingness to travel regularly between VersAbility locations and assigned Government Contract sites throughout Hampton Roads.REAL ID-compliant identification or valid U.S. Passport, or ability to obtain the required identification before the start date, for applicable military installation access.Ability to obtain and maintain required military installation/base access credentials and authorizations.Ability to obtain and maintain a Secret security clearance when required for an assigned Government Contract location.Ability to use Microsoft Office, Outlook, Teams, virtual meeting platforms, cameras, headsets, and other technology necessary for remote interpreting.PreferredBachelor's degree in American Sign Language/English Interpretation, Interpreter Education, ASL Studies, or a related field.Two to three years of professional interpreting experience.National Interpreter Certification (NIC).Experience interpreting in employment, government, healthcare, educational, technical, or other professional environments.ScheduleThis is a full-time, permanent position working 40 hours per week. Monday–Friday | 8:00 a.m.–4:30 p.m. Because interpreting needs occur across different VersAbility programs, locations, and time zones, candidates must be flexible to adjust their schedule based on employee communication needs, interpreting assignments, orientations, meetings, training, organizational events, and operational requirements. Regular local travel throughout Hampton Roads is required. The position will also provide virtual interpreting support for geographically dispersed VersAbility locations, including locations such as San Diego and Hawaii.Work Environment & Physical RequirementsThis is a dynamic interpreting position rather than a role based in one work environment. Assignments may take place in professional offices, orientation and training environments, VersAbility facilities, community locations, Government Contract sites, military installations, and virtual environments.Depending on the assignment, work environments may include changing lighting, varying temperatures, moderate to loud noise, distractions, outdoor conditions, or industrial and operational settings. Some assignments may involve lengthy, complex, technical, sensitive, or emotionally demanding communication.The position requires sustained concentration and visual attention, continuous and repetitive use of the hands, fingers, wrists, arms, and shoulders for ASL, and the upper-body stamina necessary for extended interpreting assignments. Regular travel between work locations and frequent entry and exit from a vehicle are also required.Candidates must be able to perform the essential duties and physical requirements of the position, with or without reasonable accommodation. VersAbility Resources provides reasonable accommodations in accordance with applicable law.Why Join Us?Help build something new. You will step into a newly created permanent role and help strengthen how VersAbility provides consistent communication access across the organization.Make an impact employees can experience every day. Your work will help Deaf and hard-of-hearing employees more fully access workplace communication, training, meetings, resources, and opportunities.Build continuity and trust. As a staff interpreter, you will have the opportunity to become familiar with our employees, terminology, teams, and work environments—supporting more consistent communication over time.Experience variety in your work. Assignments may take you from orientations and employee meetings to Government Contract environments, training sessions, virtual meetings, and other workplace settings.Use your profession to advance inclusion. Your expertise will directly support VersAbility's commitment to creating workplaces where employees of all abilities have meaningful access and opportunities to thrive.Grow with the role. As a new position within VersAbility, you will have the opportunity to help establish strong practices and contribute your professional perspective as our interpreting needs evolve.How to ApplyApply online through VersAbility Resources' careers site. If you need assistance or reasonable accommodation during the application process, please contact us at wehire@versability.org.Equal Opportunity EmployerVersAbility Resources is an Equal Opportunity Employer committed to providing fair and equitable employment opportunities. We consider qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, or any other protected characteristic under applicable law. We value diversity and encourage applicants of all backgrounds to apply. Certain positions are performed under the federal AbilityOne Program and are subject to applicable contractual and program requirements.

jobs.description: Employer: The Arc Ocean County Chapter Expires: 10/14/2026 DescriptionTurn Everyday Activities Into Meaningful OpportunitiesThe Arc of Ocean County is seeking an energetic and compassionate Program Instructor to join our Adult Day Program in Lakewood. This role is centered on creating purposeful daily experiences that help adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities strengthen life skills, explore interests, build relationships, and participate more fully in their communities.You'll have the opportunity to combine instruction, encouragement, and hands-on experiences to help individuals work toward their personal goals. Whether you're leading a structured activity, supporting a community outing, or helping someone master a new skill, your work can make each day an opportunity for growth and greater independence.
